sources.entry: AirStats - Menu bar system monitor for CPU, memory, GPU, network, disk, battery, temperature, and processes, with a desktop widget.

summary.one_liner: AirStats is a lightweight macOS menu bar system monitor that shows CPU, memory, GPU, network, disk, battery, temperature, process and host statistics, plus a desktop widget.
summary.what_it_does: It reads CPU, memory, GPU, network, disk, battery, temperature, process and host statistics from the kernel and displays them in three places: the menu bar itself, a panel that drops down when the status item is clicked, and a desktop widget that can stay on screen. It reads system data through Mach, IOKit, sysctl and CoreWLAN. It has no Dock icon. The README says it is designed to use only a few megabytes of memory and a fraction of one CPU core. It can check for updates weekly via Sparkle, which installs only when the user approves, and both behaviors can be turned off in General settings.
use_cases: monitor CPU and memory usage from the menu bar
watch network, disk and battery status on a Mac
check Mac temperature and GPU load
keep a system stats widget on the desktop
find which processes are using resources
notable: Very low resource use: README claims a few megabytes of memory and a fraction of a percent of one core
Menu bar, dropdown panel and desktop widget views of the same stats
Signed and notarized downloads, with Homebrew cask install option
Built-in Sparkle auto-update that asks before installing
AirStatKit core has no SwiftUI or AppKit imports, so tests run headless
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later and Apple silicon
Building from source requires Xcode 26 or later for the macOS 26 SDK (Liquid Glass)
Ad-hoc signed local builds will not run if they were downloaded from the internet
keywords: see cpu usage in menu bar
